newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: KOF says Swiss export outlook remains uncertain.
newsitem.headline: KOF says Swiss export outlook remains uncertain.

text.p: The Swiss Institute for Business Cycle Research (KOF) expects the economy to recover slowly later this year but said the outlook for Switzerland's export-dependent growth would depend largely on the trend in Europe.
Surprisingly, the Swiss franc's declines in the first quarter of this year failed to boost exports, which showed instead showed a weaker to stagnant trend, the KOF said.

"What for many people was surprising was the export activity. One would have expected the Swiss franc's decline to have had a beneficial impact. But industrial orders tended to decline," Bernd Schips, KOF managing director, told reporters.
He said Swiss franc weakness in the first quarter was more pronounced versus the dollar than the mark, while most Swiss exports go to Europe.
He said exporters also likely used the Swiss franc's decline to improve their margins, rather than as an opportunity to lower export prices.
In the main European market, other countries' economies also remained mostly weak, which meant that orders for the Swiss capital goods industry were slow.
The Swiss franc began 1997 at 1.34 to the dollar and bottomed out in early March just over 1.49 francs. The dollar has since dropped back to around 1.4450.
The mark began the year at 87.00 Swiss centimes, peaked at roughly 87.70 in late February and early March, and is now trading closer to 84.70 centimes.
The Swiss National Bank has stressed in the past that its generous monetary policy was aimed at what it saw as an overvalued Swiss franc, which it says hurts exports.
In its general prognosis, KOF said it did not expect the SNB to ease rates further in the current cycle. Instead it was more apt to tighten once the economic recovery began.
While export activity slowed, the trend in domestic industry saw some improvement, albeit from very low levels.
It also saw expected further declines in jobs, saying that personnel capacity at Swiss businesses remained higher than technical capacity.
KOF expects Swiss first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) to fall 0.4 percent on a real, annualised basis versus the 1996 first quarter.
Versus the fourth quarter of 1996, first-quarter GDP is expected to be up 0.5 percent, it said.
KOF forecast GDP growth in the second quarter as flat versus second-quarter 1996. Third-quarter GDP was seen up 0.7 percent, and fourth quarter up 0.9 percent against the comparable 1996 quarters.
The Swiss Federal Office for Economic Policy is expected to report first-quarter GDP sometime between June 10 and June 15.
